findings.body: Previously a synchronous `getCalendar` throw was caught by the enclosing try/catch and logged via `logger.error`. Now the callback returns a promise that `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores, so any rejection escapes the try/catch entirely, producing an unhandled promise rejection (process crash under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw`), and the cancellation work is fire-and-forget so the function proceeds before deletions complete.
findings.failure_mode: Errors bypass the intended error handling, causing unhandled promise rejections and silently incomplete calendar/video cancellations.
findings.impact: Previously a synchronous `getCalendar` throw was caught by the enclosing try/catch and logged via `logger.error`. Now the callback returns a promise that `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores, so any rejection escapes the try/catch entirely, producing an unhandled promise rejection (process crash under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw`), and the cancellation work is fire-and-forget so the function proceeds before deletions complete.
findings.root_cause: The patch made the forEach callback async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar, but forEach does not await or surface promises returned by its callback.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `forEach(async ...)` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` (or a for...of loop with await) inside the existing try block so errors are caught and deletions complete before continuing.
findings.title: Async forEach callback makes surrounding try/catch dead code and turns errors into unhandled rejections
findings.trigger: A Vital reschedule runs for a booking whose calendar/video references exist and `getCalendar` (now async, backed by dynamic `import()`) rejects, or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` throws inside the callback.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 125 shows `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` verbatim. The callback is async but forEach ignores returned promises, so rejections from await getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting escape the surrounding try/catch at line 124. This is a real defect introduced by the patch.

findings.body: The enclosing try/catch that calls `logger.error` can no longer catch these errors because `forEach` discards the returned promise; rejections become unhandled (crashing Node under default settings) and cancellations are fire-and-forget, so the API can return success while third-party events remain undeleted.
findings.failure_mode: Intended error handling is silently bypassed; unhandled rejections and incomplete cancellations occur.

findings.root_cause: Converting the forEach callback to async without switching to an awaited iteration construct; forEach never awaits callback promises.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` or a for...of loop with await inside the try block so rejections are caught and awaited.

raw_findings.trigger: A user reschedules a booking whose references include a calendar or video entry, and the now-async `getCalendar` (backed by dynamic `import()`) rejects or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejects.

raw_findings.body: The stated goal of async/lazy imports is defeated because every app package is still loaded whenever appStore is imported, and a rejected import promise that no caller ever awaits produces an unhandled promise rejection, which terminates the Node process under the default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` behavior.
raw_findings.failure_mode: All app modules load on first appStore import, and any load failure for an unused app crashes the process via unhandled rejection.
raw_findings.impact: The stated goal of async/lazy imports is defeated because every app package is still loaded whenever appStore is imported, and a rejected import promise that no caller ever awaits produces an unhandled promise rejection, which terminates the Node process under the default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` behavior.
raw_findings.root_cause: Object-literal properties hold eagerly-started top-level `import()` promises instead of lazy import factories.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Store lazy thunks (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke/await them at access sites (e.g., `await appStore[key]?.()`), so imports only run on demand and rejections are always observed by a caller.
raw_findings.title: Top-level import() promises in appStore load all apps eagerly and risk unhandled rejections for never-accessed apps
raw_findings.trigger: Any module imports `@calcom/app-store` (e.g., videoClient, handlePayment); all 28 `import()` calls begin executing at module evaluation. If any single app module fails to load at runtime (missing dependency, top-level throw from misconfiguration), its promise rejects even if that app is never accessed or awaited.

raw_findings.body: A rejected, never-awaited promise triggers Node's unhandledRejection handling (process crash under default settings) during routine connected-calendar listing, and the `calendar` field consumers now silently receive a Promise instead of a Calendar unless they remember to await it.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Potential unhandled promise rejection and a promise-typed field masquerading as a Calendar value.
raw_findings.impact: A rejected, never-awaited promise triggers Node's unhandledRejection handling (process crash under default settings) during routine connected-calendar listing, and the `calendar` field consumers now silently receive a Promise instead of a Calendar unless they remember to await it.
raw_findings.root_cause: Making getCalendar async changed its return type to a promise while a synchronous caller continues to create and sometimes discard that promise unhandled.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update getCalendarCredentials to either await/handle the getCalendar promise (attach a `.catch`) or only create the promise when `app.variant === "calendar"`, and rename the field (e.g., `calendarPromise`) or make getCalendarCredentials async to make the new asynchrony explicit at call sites.
raw_findings.title: getCalendarCredentials still calls now-async getCalendar synchronously, discarding possibly-rejecting promises
raw_findings.trigger: `getCalendarCredentials` in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts (unchanged, still synchronous) calls `getCalendar(credential)` at line 28 without await; when `app.variant !== "calendar"` the created promise is dropped, and if the underlying dynamic import for that app fails to load, the discarded promise rejects with no handler ever attached.

raw_findings.root_cause: The rewrite of the appStore map dropped the underscore prefix from the example module path in the comment.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the commented line to `// example: import("./_example"),` to match the actual directory name.

validated_findings.impact: A rejected, never-awaited promise triggers Node's unhandledRejection handling (process crash under default settings) during routine connected-calendar listing, and the `calendar` field consumers now silently receive a Promise instead of a Calendar unless they remember to await it.
validated_findings.root_cause: Making getCalendar async changed its return type to a promise while a synchronous caller continues to create and sometimes discard that promise unhandled.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update getCalendarCredentials to either await/handle the getCalendar promise (attach a `.catch`) or only create the promise when `app.variant === "calendar"`, and rename the field (e.g., `calendarPromise`) or make getCalendarCredentials async to make the new asynchrony explicit at call sites.
validated_findings.title: getCalendarCredentials still calls now-async getCalendar synchronously, discarding possibly-rejecting promises
validated_findings.trigger: `getCalendarCredentials` in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts (unchanged, still synchronous) calls `getCalendar(credential)` at line 28 without await; when `app.variant !== "calendar"` the created promise is dropped, and if the underlying dynamic import for that app fails to load, the discarded promise rejects with no handler ever attached.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim references getCalendarCredentials at CalendarManager.ts:28 calling getCalendar synchronously. However, the provided context at CalendarManager.ts:23-135 shows line 28 calls getCalendar and line 48 shows `const calendar = await item.calendar`, indicating the promise is awaited in getConnectedCalendars. The finding mischaracterizes the actual code flow.

validated_findings.body: The import path no longer matches the pre-existing `./_example` directory (the removed line was `import * as example from "./_example";`), so uncommenting produces a module-not-found build error and misleads developers about the example app's location.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale/incorrect reference comment that breaks when followed literally.
validated_findings.impact: The import path no longer matches the pre-existing `./_example` directory (the removed line was `import * as example from "./_example";`), so uncommenting produces a module-not-found build error and misleads developers about the example app's location.
validated_findings.root_cause: The rewrite of the appStore map dropped the underscore prefix from the example module path in the comment.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change the commented line to `// example: import("./_example"),` to match the actual directory name.
validated_findings.title: Commented example import references "./example" instead of the actual "./_example" directory
validated_findings.trigger: A developer uncomments the example entry to scaffold a new app, following the pattern documented in the app-store docs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The comment `// example: import("./example")` references ./example while the old code used ./_example. However, this is a commented-out line that serves as documentation/template. The actual _example directory existence is not verified in context, and the impact is minimal (developer inconvenience if they uncomment). Low severity doc issue with uncertain factual basis.
